title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page updated 4 Oct 2026). Level AA ratios of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; large text is 18 pt, or 14 pt bold; ratios are not rounded; logotypes and incidental text are exempt but brand guidelines do not exempt other text; the contrast formula and the 1:1 to 21:1 range

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 3:1 for icons, chart lines and other graphics needed to understand content, and for controls; exceptions for decorative graphics, logos, photos and flags, and graphics whose information is also given as text

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
supports: Opened with WebFetch. W3C Recommendation dated 12 December 2024; 1.4.1 Use of Color (colour must not be the only visual means of conveying information); 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced) at 7:1 and 4.5:1; 1.4.12 Text Spacing values

title: Images Tutorial
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page updated 8 Apr 2026). How to write text alternatives for informative, decorative, functional and complex images and images of text; alt text depends on context

title: Guide to the ADA Accessibility Standards, Chapter 7: Signs
supports: Opened with WebFetch (guide dated August 2022). Minimum visual character heights by mounting height and viewing distance; light-on-dark or dark-on-light contrast with no set minimum; non-glare finish; no italic, script or decorative letters; which signs need raised characters and braille; tactile sign mounting at 48 to 60 inches; 6-inch pictogram field

title: Color Blindness
publisher: National Eye Institute (US National Institutes of Health)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 5 Nov 2025). About 1 in 12 men have colour vision deficiency; red-green is the most common type

title: A new era for inclusion begins: the European Accessibility Act enters into force
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 27 Jun 2025). European Accessibility Act requirements apply from 28 June 2025 and cover e-commerce, e-books, banking, transport and other products and services

title: Accessible communication formats
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 17 Jun 2026). Large print means 16 point and above; 50 to 65 characters per line and never more than 80; cut text before cutting type size; do not make large print by enlarging on a photocopier

title: Butterick's Practical Typography: Summary of key rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch; author and edition confirmed on the site's home page. 10 to 12 point body text in print and 15 to 25 pixels on the web; line spacing 120 to 145% of the point size; 45 to 90 characters per line; capitals for less than one line; no underlining; centred text used sparingly

title: Visual Hierarchy in UX: Definition (Kelley Gordon, 17 Jan 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Hierarchy comes from colour and contrast, scale and grouping; suggests no more than three type sizes; proximity, white space and common regions make groups; the squint or blur test

title: Interaction of Color, 50th Anniversary Edition (Josef Albers)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The book, first published 1963, 50th anniversary edition 2013; teaches through colour studies how colours interact and how we perceive them

title: The Non-Designer's Design Book, 4th Edition (Robin Williams)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 4th edition published 19 Nov 2014; chapters on proximity, alignment, repetition and contrast

title: Instagram Help Center: photo resolution and aspect ratios (article 1631821640426723; descriptive title)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (the help.instagram.com copy of the same article loads no text for the fetch tool). Widths from 320 to 1080 pixels; aspect ratios from 1.91:1 to 4:5; portrait 1080 x 1350; landscape 1080 x 566; other ratios are cropped

title: Meta Ads Guide: Instagram Stories image ad specs
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). 9:16 ratio, 1440 x 2560 recommended; keep about 14% at the top, 35% at the bottom and 6% at each side free of text and logos; minimum width 500 pixels

title: Pinterest product specs
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). Standard Pins at 2:3 or 1000 x 1500 pixels, taller Pins may be cut off in feeds; PNG or JPEG; carousel Pins of 2 to 5 images at 1:1 or 2:3

title: Set Trim Size, Bleed, and Margins
supports: Opened with WebFetch. One printer's published bleed rule: 0.125 in (3.2 mm) past the trim on the top, bottom and outside edges; minimum outside margins of 0.25 in without bleed and 0.375 in with bleed; gutter grows with page count

title: Domestic Mail Manual 101: Physical Standards for Commercial Letters, Flats and Parcels (section 6.2.2, postcard dimensions)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Card-price postcards must be rectangular, at least 5 x 3.5 in and 0.007 in thick, and at most 6 x 4.25 in and 0.016 in thick

title: How to prepare perfect print files for print-on-demand (Marianna Zvaigzne, 28 Jul 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Printful's own file rules: 150 to 300 DPI with 150 as its usual target and 300 for small detailed items; PNG or JPEG, PNG only for embroidery; sRGB rather than CMYK files; transparent backgrounds; a 12 x 16 in t-shirt print area (15 x 18 in on some DTG products); white underbase on non-white garments

title: DTG vs. screen printing (Maisha Rachmat, 23 Sep 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Vendor guide: screen printing needs one screen per colour and vendors usually cap designs at about nine colours; thin lines can clog; typical minimums of 5 to 100 units and Printful's from 500; DTG has no minimum and handles gradients; screen prints usually last longer; Printful's own wash-durability claim for DTG

title: Color matching guide for print-on-demand products (Una Savčenko, 12 Jun 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. RGB covers more colours than CMYK so neons and very saturated shades shift in print; fabric weave changes how colour looks; order samples and print a swatch sheet before selling

title: Copyright vs trademark: What every creator needs to know (Andris Mucenieks, 20 Jan 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Other businesses' logos, names, slogans, characters and song lyrics need permission; credit does not replace permission; use public domain or licensed material

title: SIL Open Font License
supports: Opened with WebFetch. OFL 1.1 (text dated 26 Feb 2007; FAQ update 7, Nov 2023): fonts may be used in posters, artwork, logos and websites with no acknowledgement required; fonts may be modified and redistributed; Reserved Font Names

title: Copyright Office Releases Part 2 of Artificial Intelligence Report (NewsNet 1060, 29 Jan 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Prompts alone do not make an AI output protectable; human expressive inputs, selection and arrangement, and real modifications can be

title: AI Act, Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Providers must mark synthetic images, audio, video and text in a machine-readable way; deployers must disclose deepfakes; lighter disclosure for evidently artistic, creative or satirical work; exception for human-reviewed text with editorial responsibility

title: AI Act, Article 113: Entry into force and application

title: Allergen guidance for food businesses
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 17 Jul 2026). The 14 allergens; for non-prepacked food, allergen information may be given verbally if a clearly visible written notice says how to get it; prepacked for direct sale food needs a full ingredients list with allergens emphasised

title: Menu Labeling Requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch (content current as of 13 Dec 2023). Chains with 20 or more locations show calories on menus and menu boards, plus a 2,000-calorie statement and a statement that written nutrition information is available; compliance date 7 May 2018
